title: Finance Analyst
location_raw: Remote, NYC or East Coast Preferred
description:
About Sparkfund

Sparkfund is the utility services company unlocking capacity on the grid. Through its Distributed Capacity Procurement (DCP) model, Sparkfund enables utilities, energy majors, and large-load customers to deploy front-of-the-meter batteries and gensets as distribution infrastructure. By adding targeted capacity exactly where and when the grid needs it most, DCP helps meet demand, support reliability, and put downward pressure on rates. Sparkfund supports program design, grid value assessment, asset host engagement, and value chain management to ensure on-time, on-budget deployment with maximum system value and lowest cost.

With more than 3,200 projects deployed across 43 states and more than 300MW of energized assets constructed, Sparkfund is transforming customer-sited assets into a valuable portfolio resource for the benefit of our society. To learn more about Sparkfund, visit sparkfund.com.

FINANCE ANALYST

Department: Finance
Reports To: Director, Corporate Finance
Location: Remote (United States); preference for candidates in the New York City metro area or elsewhere on the East Coast
Employment Type: Full-Time, Exempt
Travel: Occasional; company gatherings and team meetings

About the Role

Sparkfund prices and structures its Distributed Capacity Procurement deals using a set of programmatic pricing models, and this role is responsible for both sides of that work: building the ad hoc project finance models a deal needs when it falls outside the existing templates, and keeping the standing programmatic models accurate as cost, revenue, timing, and financing assumptions shift. You'll work from our existing model library, but you'll also be expected to build new models from scratch when a deal structure calls for something the templates don't cover.

The work sits between Finance and the teams closest to the deals. You will partner with Business Development, Program, and Project teams to source the assumptions that feed a model, test them against the underlying data, and flag anything that doesn't hold up before it reaches a pricing output. You will also translate model output into language deal teams can use when they negotiate. You will report to the Director of Corporate Finance. Success in this role looks like a maintained set of pricing models that are accurate and able tohold up under review from Finance leadership and deal counterparts.

How We Work at Sparkfund

Our values guide how we work together, make decisions, and deliver for our customers and partners. Regardless of role or level, we expect everyone at Sparkfund to demonstrate:

  • Excellence: We hold ourselves to a high standard, take pride in the quality of our work, and continuously look for ways to improve.
  • Stewardship: We take ownership of our work and make thoughtful decisions with the long-term interests of Sparkfund, our customers, our partners, and one another in mind.
  • Positivity: We bring a constructive, solutions-oriented mindset to our work and contribute to an environment where people can collaborate, learn, and do their best work.

These values are part of how we evaluate success at Sparkfund, alongside the skills, competencies, and results required for each role.

What You'll Do

Pricing and Financial Modeling

  • Build, audit, and maintain the programmatic pricing models used to structure and price deals across Sparkfund's DCP programs
  • Update and refine existing models as program economics, deal structures, or market conditions change
  • Build bespoke financial models for one-off pricing structures or deal structures that fall outside existing templates

Cross-Functional Assumption Validation

  • Partner with Business Development, Program, and Project teams to source the cost, revenue, timing, and financing assumptions that feed pricing models
  • Validate assumptions against underlying source data and flag discrepancies before they reach a pricing output
  • Translate model outputs into terms non-finance stakeholders can use to structure and negotiate deals

What We're Looking For

  • 1–3 years of experience in financial modeling, corporate finance, or a related quantitative role
  • Strong technical modeling skills, including building, auditing, and troubleshooting complex Excel models from scratch
  • Working knowledge of DCF analysis, capital stack construction (debt, equity, mezzanine), and discount rate and cost of capital concepts, with fluency in IRR, NPV, and other return metrics used to evaluate deal economics
  • Strong attention to detail and comfort validating assumptions across multiple sources
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to translate model output for people who don't work in finance
  • Bachelor's degree in finance, economics, or another quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience

Nice to Have

  • Familiarity with project finance structures or energy asset modeling
  • Experience in infrastructure, energy, or utility-facing businesses
  • Experience building models that support live deal negotiations

What Will Help You Succeed

  • Analytical rigor: You build models and analyses that hold up under review. You check your work before you share it and you catch inconsistencies in the data underneath.
  • Assumption validation: You are comfortable going to other teams for the inputs you need, pressure-testing what you get back, and raising a discrepancy before it lands in a pricing output.
  • Communication clarity: You can walk someone outside Finance through what a model says and what it means for a decision they need to make.
  • Reliability: You deliver recurring work on time and raise a risk to a deadline early rather than at the deadline.

Compensation

The expected base pay range for this role is $81,000–$125,000 per year. This range reflects the span of base pay across the geographic markets where Sparkfund hires for this role, and the range applicable to a given candidate will depend on where they are located. For candidates based in New York City, the expected base pay range is $101,000–$125,000 per year.

Individual placement within the range depends on work location, prior experience, technical capabilities, core competencies, positional scope, internal alignment, and other relevant business factors.

Where applicable, this position may also be eligible for discretionary bonus or incentive compensation. Any such compensation is separate from base salary and is not guaranteed. Eligibility, amounts, and payment are subject to applicable plan terms, company performance, individual performance, and other business considerations.

Benefits

Sparkfund offers a competitive benefits package designed to support employees both at work and outside of it, including:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance
  • 401(k) with 2% employer match
  • Flexible vacation policy with a strong emphasis on work-life balance
  • Federal holidays and Flexible Fridays, including half-day Fridays each week
  • 12 weeks of gender-neutral paid caregiver leave
  • One-time work-from-home stipend for eligible remote roles
  • $100 monthly phone and Wi-Fi allowance

Work Environment

Sparkfund is a remote-first company with a distributed workforce and emerging hub offices in Denver, Minneapolis, and Washington, DC. This role is performed remotely with occasional travel for team meetings, company gatherings, and other business needs. We are open to candidates anywhere in the United States where Sparkfund is registered to employ, with a preference for candidates in the New York City metro area or elsewhere on the East Coast for time zone overlap with the Finance and deal teams.

No significant physical requirements apply beyond standard office work. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Sparkfund is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing an inclusive and welcoming environment for all employees and applicants. We do not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Sparkfund also provides reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and for sincerely held religious beliefs or practices, in all phases of the hiring process and throughout employment. If you need an accommodation, please let us know.

Disclaimer

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications. Duties, responsibilities, and requirements may change at any time based on business needs. We encourage individuals of all backgrounds and experiences to apply — even if you do not meet every listed qualification — as skills and competencies can develop in different ways.

About the Role

Sparkfund is looking for a Senior Manager, Project Management with significant construction project delivery experience and a background in the energy industry to lead the planning and execution of a portfolio of complex energy and infrastructure projects.

This is a construction and energy project delivery role. Candidates must have direct experience managing the execution of construction projects involving energy infrastructure, electrical systems,, controls, distributed generation, battery energy storage, solar,or comparable energy technologies.

The Senior Manager will oversee multiple customer EPC projects, directly manage Project Managers and Project Coordinators, and serve as a primary point of contact for customer stakeholders. This role is accountable for project execution across scope, schedule, budget, safety, quality, and customer expectations.

This position must be based in the Minneapolis area. While Sparkfund operates as a remote-first company, this role will have regular engagement with our Minneapolis hub and local team, in addition to travel to project sites.

Success in this role requires someone who understands how construction and energy projects move from development into field execution and can lead both a complex project portfolio and the people responsible for delivering it.

How We Work at Sparkfund

Our values shape how we work, make decisions, and show up for our customers and each other. They are also part of how we evaluate success at Sparkfund.

Excellence

We hold ourselves to high standards and continuously look for ways to improve.

In this role, Excellence means bringing rigor to project planning and execution, maintaining high standards for safety and quality, anticipating issues before they become problems, and ensuring that our work is something we’re proud to put our name on.

Stewardship

We take ownership, follow through on our commitments, and make thoughtful decisions with the long term in mind.

For this role, Stewardship means treating customer relationships, project budgets, schedules, company resources, and safety responsibilities with care and accountability. It also means balancing the needs of the customer, our project teams, and Sparkfund when making decisions.

Positivity

We approach challenges constructively, assume positive intent, support one another, and bring solutions.

For this role, Positivity means remaining steady when projects become difficult, communicating directly and respectfully, helping teams work through challenges, and creating an environment where people can solve problems together.

What You’ll Do

Lead Construction & Portfolio Delivery

  • Oversee the planning, coordination, construction, and delivery of a portfolio of customer EPC and energy infrastructure projects
  • Manage portfolio performance across scope, schedule, budget, safety, quality, and customer requirements
  • Monitor construction schedules, project milestones, cost forecasts, risks, change orders, and delivery dependencies
  • Identify potential schedule delays, budget concerns, site issues, and construction risks early and drive resolution
  • Lead the resolution of escalated project and construction issues in partnership with internal teams, contractors, vendors, and customers
  • Own portfolio-level budgeting, cost forecasting, financial performance, and variance management
  • Review and administer project contracts, scopes of work, change orders, and construction-related commitments
  • Partner with Project Development and Commercial teams during early project stages to evaluate constructability, execution risk, cost assumptions, and delivery requirements

Lead & Develop the Team

  • Directly manage and develop Project Managers and Project Coordinators responsible for construction and project delivery
  • Set clear priorities, expectations, performance standards, and accountability across the team
  • Provide ongoing coaching, feedback, and professional development support
  • Create consistency across project planning, documentation, financial management, risk management, and customer communication
  • Partner with the broader Project Delivery organization to strengthen project management tools, processes, and operating practices

Build Strong Customer & Stakeholder Relationships

  • Serve as a trusted Sparkfund point of contact for customer stakeholders throughout project execution
  • Maintain strong customer relationships and ensure alignment with project commitments and expectations
  • Communicate construction progress, schedules, risks, delays, budget impacts, and resolution plans clearly and proactively
  • Present portfolio and project information to internal leaders, customers, contractors, and executive stakeholders
  • Translate technical and construction information into clear, practical updates for non-technical audiences
  • Organize and deliver weekly, quarterly, and annual reporting on portfolio and project performance

Partner Across Sparkfund

  • Work closely with Project Delivery, Programs, Project Development, Commercial Solutions, EH&S, Finance, and Customer Experience
  • Provide project delivery expertise related to energy efficiency, distributed energy resources, and sustainable infrastructure
  • Help ensure customer commitments made during development and contracting can be successfully executed in the field
  • Align commercial, technical, financial, safety, and operational requirements throughout the project lifecycle

What We’re Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of construction project management, construction management, EPC project delivery, or trade contracting experience
  • Direct professional experience delivering energy or energy-related construction projects
  • Experience delivering projects involving one or more of the following: electrical systems, HVAC, building controls, distributed generation, battery energy storage, solar, EV charging, generators, energy efficiency, or comparable energy infrastructure
  • Experience managing multiple concurrent construction projects or a portfolio of projects through execution
  • Experience directly managing Project Managers, Construction Managers, Project Coordinators, or similar project delivery professionals
  • Strong construction scheduling, budgeting, cost forecasting, risk management, and change management experience
  • Experience reviewing and administering construction contracts, scopes of work, change orders, and project requirements
  • Experience working directly with contractors, subcontractors, vendors, and field-based project teams
  • Demonstrated ability to manage customer relationships and communicate effectively with executive stakeholders
  • Strong understanding of job-site safety and construction safety practices
  • Proficiency with project management software and cloud-based information management tools
  • Must be based in the Minneapolis area
  • Ability to travel approximately 10–30%, depending on project portfolio

This role requires direct construction and energy project delivery experience. General project or program management experience in financial services, healthcare, software, manufacturing, or other non-construction environments does not substitute for the required construction and energy experience.

Nice to Have

  • Experience delivering EPC projects
  • Battery energy storage, utility, renewable energy, distributed energy, or energy services experience
  • Experience using Procore or comparable construction management software
  • Project development experience in clean energy, resilience, distributed energy, or energy efficiency
  • Experience working with engineering firms, general contractors, specialty contractors, and equipment manufacturers
  • Familiarity with Salesforce, Google Workspace, Microsoft applications, and Slack
  • Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified Construction Manager (CCM), or another relevant certification
  • OSHA, NFPA, or other construction and safety training or certifications

What Will Help You Succeed

Portfolio Leadership

You can step above individual projects and manage the health of an entire portfolio, balancing scope, schedule, budget, safety, quality, customer expectations, and risk across multiple projects simultaneously.

Construction & Energy Expertise

You understand what it takes to execute construction projects in the field and can apply that experience within energy and infrastructure environments. You’re comfortable engaging with contractors, technical teams, site personnel, customers, and internal stakeholders.

People Leadership

You set clear expectations, create accountability, and develop Project Managers and Coordinators through coaching, feedback, and ongoing support.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

You build credibility with customers and communicate project status, risks, challenges, and solutions clearly, including with senior and executive stakeholders.

Decision-Making Under Ambiguity

You can make sound decisions when information is incomplete, prioritize competing needs, and keep projects moving in a dynamic environment.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

You work effectively across technical, commercial, financial, operational, and customer-facing teams and understand that successful project delivery requires alignment across the organization.

Compensation

The approved salary range for this position is $165,000–$209,000, based on experience, qualifications, and location.

Where applicable, this position may also be eligible for discretionary bonus or incentive compensation. Any such compensation is separate from base salary and is not guaranteed. Eligibility, amounts, and payment are subject to applicable plan terms, company performance, individual performance, and other business considerations.

Benefits

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance
  • 401(k) plan with a 2% employer match
  • Flexible vacation policy
  • Paid federal holidays
  • Flexible Fridays, with half-day Fridays every week

Work Environment

Sparkfund is a remote-first company with emerging hub offices in Denver, Minneapolis, and Washington, DC.

This position is remote-flexible but must be based in the Minneapolis area, with regular engagement with Sparkfund’s Minneapolis hub and local team.

Travel within the continental United States is expected approximately 10–30%, depending on portfolio needs, including periodic visits to active construction and project sites.

SENIOR POWER SYSTEMS ENGINEER

Department: Programs

Reports To: Director, Power Systems Engineering

Location: Remote, U.S.

Employment Type: Full-Time, Exempt

Travel: Approximately 15% for utility partner meetings, project sites, company gatherings, industry conferences, and sales visits

About Sparkfund

Sparkfund is the utility services company unlocking capacity on the grid. Through its Distributed Capacity Procurement (DCP) model, Sparkfund enables utilities, energy majors, and large-load customers to deploy front-of-the-meter batteries and gensets as distribution infrastructure. By adding targeted capacity exactly where and when the grid needs it most, DCP helps meet demand, support reliability, and put downward pressure on rates. Sparkfund supports program design, grid value assessment, asset host engagement, and value chain management to ensure on-time, on-budget deployment with maximum system value and lowest cost.

With more than 3,200 projects deployed across 43 states and more than 300MW of energized assets constructed, Sparkfund is transforming customer-sited assets into a valuable portfolio resource for the benefit of our society. To learn more about Sparkfund, visit sparkfund.com.

About the Role

The electric grid is evolving faster than it has in decades. Utilities are navigating significant load growth driven by electrification, data centers, distributed energy resources, battery energy storage, and other emerging technologies while continuing to balance reliability, affordability, and infrastructure constraints.

Sparkfund is looking for a Senior Power Systems Engineer to help execute the technical engineering strategy behind our Distributed Capacity Procurement programs.

In this role, you'll serve as a technical subject matter expert across distribution system planning, utility operations, DER integration, interconnection, controls, operational technology, and grid modernization. You'll work directly with utility and large electricity-consumer customers to identify grid needs, evaluate distributed capacity opportunities, and help ensure DCP technologies can be integrated safely, effectively, and at scale.

You'll partner closely with Commercialization, Program Management, Project Delivery, and utility technical teams to evaluate use cases, develop integration strategies, and translate complex engineering requirements into practical solutions.

Direct experience working with electric utilities on distribution planning and interconnection is required for this role. You’ll be working closely with utility engineers to deploy distributed energy resources in their service territory.

This is an individual contributor role with significant technical ownership and no direct reports.

How We Work at Sparkfund

Our values guide how we work together, make decisions, and deliver for our customers and partners. Regardless of role or level, we expect everyone at Sparkfund to demonstrate:

  • Excellence: We hold ourselves to a high standard, take pride in the quality of our work, and continuously look for ways to improve.
  • Stewardship: We take ownership of our work and make thoughtful decisions with the long-term interests of Sparkfund, our customers, our partners, and one another in mind.
  • Positivity: We bring a constructive, solutions-oriented mindset to our work and contribute to an environment where people can collaborate, learn, and do their best work.

These values are part of how we evaluate success at Sparkfund, alongside the skills, competencies, and results required for each role.

What You'll Do

Distribution System Analysis

  • Evaluate utility power-flow analysis capabilities, tools, techniques, and outputs and their application to grid needs assessments, hosting-capacity studies, and locational value determinations.
  • Perform operational technology maturity assessments for utility partners, evaluating DERMS, ADMS, SCADA, DMS, and OMS capabilities against the requirements for DCP fleet dispatch, monitoring, and market participation.
  • Help utility partners identify where existing planning, operational, and technology capabilities may need to evolve to support distributed capacity at scale.

DCP Asset Interconnection and Integration

  • Support the development and review of DER interconnection engineering deliverables, including single-line diagrams, site plans, preliminary protection coordination settings, effective grounding calculations, commissioning plans, and IEEE 1547 conformity assessments.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline and improve utility processes that may otherwise slow or constrain DER deployment.
  • Inform the technical design of distributed energy technologies, including battery energy storage systems, to support deployment at speed and scale while balancing schedule, budget, and operational requirements.
  • Identify appropriate distribution-system integration study processes for DCP use cases, including traditional distribution system planning, non-wires alternatives, and DER interconnection.
  • Contribute to communications and network architecture for DER site integration, including DNP3, SunSpec Modbus, IEEE 2030.5, data-point mapping, polling requirements, and cybersecurity considerations.
  • Develop OT integration roadmaps and architecture recommendations that help utility partners move from current-state capabilities toward DCP-ready dispatch and telemetry.
  • Define end-to-end controls and communications architectures required for market participation, including communication pathways, DERMS integration points, and site-controller dispatch interfaces.

Opportunity Evaluation

  • Help develop Sparkfund's portfolio of distributed energy resource use cases from both a distribution-system and electricity-consumer perspective across front-of-the-meter, behind-the-meter, and across-the-meter applications.
  • Contribute to cost-benefit analyses for DCP deployments by evaluating technical data and informing assumptions related to capital costs, operating costs, and distribution-system value streams.
  • Help internal teams and utility partners understand how technical, operational, and economic considerations interact when evaluating deployment opportunities.

Wholesale Market Interface

  • Maintain current working knowledge of energy-storage registration, telemetry, dispatch, and settlement requirements across relevant ISO/RTO markets.
  • Track rule changes and implementation timelines that may affect DCP asset participation.
  • Translate wholesale market mechanics, including co-optimization rules, DER participation frameworks, and telemetry requirements, into practical engineering and program-design inputs.

What Makes This Role Unique

  • Work directly with electric utilities across different markets, regulatory environments, and technical landscapes.
  • Help shape how distributed energy resources and battery storage are integrated into modern distribution systems.
  • Solve real-world engineering challenges involving grid capacity, reliability, interconnection, controls, and operational technology.
  • Work at the intersection of utility engineering, emerging technology, wholesale markets, and commercial program development.
  • Build technical approaches and engineering processes designed to scale across multiple utility territories rather than solving only one-off projects.
  • Contribute to programs designed to help utilities address growing capacity needs without relying solely on traditional infrastructure investments.

What We're Looking For

  • Bachelor of Electrical Engineering degree from a university with an accredited program.
  • 5+ years of experience in power system engineering, distribution engineering, DER integration, or a closely related field
  • Experience working directly with electric utilities on interconnection and distribution planning
  • Experience with distributed energy technologies such as battery energy storage, solar, or rotating machine generation.
  • Familiarity with engineering simulation tools and power-system modeling software
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with utility technical teams and manage complex engineering workstreams
  • Experience with utility codes and standards for medium- and low-voltage electric distribution equipment
  • Experience with utility safety practices and standards, including the National Electrical Safety Code (NESC/IEEE C2)
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex technical concepts and engineering tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders

Nice to Have

  • Experience developing or improving business processes, operating practices, or change-management initiatives
  • Familiarity with cybersecurity considerations for utility operational technology, including NERC CIP compliance frameworks and BES Cyber System applicability
  • Background in battery energy storage system design and integration
  • Experience with BESS project-finance technical due diligence, including technical reports or bankability documentation
  • Familiarity with DER aggregation participation models related to FERC Order 2222
  • Experience working in a program-based or multi-site deployment environment

What Will Help You Succeed

  • Technical Authority: You can serve as a trusted engineering voice on distribution planning, operations, DER design, interconnection, and code compliance while making sound technical decisions and clearly communicating engineering tradeoffs.
  • Utility Technical Engagement: You understand how utilities evaluate interconnection applications and system impacts and can identify practical strategies to improve approval pathways and reduce cycle time.
  • Engineering Scalability: You think in systems rather than one-off solutions and can develop engineering standards, processes, and approaches that scale across utility territories and program types.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: You work effectively across Commercialization, Program Management, Project Delivery, and technical teams and understand how engineering decisions affect commercial and operational outcomes.
  • Problem-Solving Under Complexity: You're comfortable navigating utility-specific requirements, jurisdictional differences, evolving codes, and emerging technologies while finding practical solutions to complex technical challenges.

Compensation

The anticipated base salary range for this position is $119,000–$142,000 per year.

Individual placement within the range depends on experience, qualifications, technical capabilities, geographic location, internal alignment, and other relevant business considerations.

Where applicable, this position may also be eligible for discretionary bonus or incentive compensation. Any such compensation is separate from base salary and is not guaranteed. Eligibility, amounts, and payment are subject to applicable plan terms, company performance, individual performance, and other business considerations.

Benefits

Sparkfund offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support employees both at work and outside of it, including:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance
  • 401(k) with 2% employer match
  • Flexible vacation policy with a strong emphasis on work-life balance
  • Federal holidays and Flexible Fridays, including half-day Fridays each week
  • 12 weeks of gender-neutral paid caregiver leave
  • One-time work-from-home stipend
  • $100 monthly phone and Wi-Fi allowance

Work Environment

Sparkfund is a remote-first company with a distributed workforce and emerging hub offices in Denver, Minneapolis, and Washington, DC. This role is performed remotely with approximately 15% travel for utility partner meetings, project sites, company gatherings, industry conferences, sales visits, and other business needs.

No significant physical requirements apply beyond standard office work. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the role.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Sparkfund is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing an inclusive and welcoming environment for all employees and applicants. We do not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Sparkfund also provides reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and for sincerely held religious beliefs or practices, in all phases of the hiring process and throughout employment. If you need an accommodation, please let us know.

title: Vice President, Electric Cooperative Markets
description:
About Sparkfund

Sparkfund is the utility services company unlocking capacity on the grid. Through its Distributed Capacity Procurement (DCP) model, Sparkfund enables utilities, energy majors, and large-load customers to deploy front-of-the-meter batteries and gensets as distribution infrastructure. By adding targeted capacity exactly where and when the grid needs it most, DCP helps meet demand, support reliability, and put downward pressure on rates. Sparkfund supports program design, grid value assessment, asset host engagement, and value chain management to ensure on-time, on-budget deployment with maximum system value and lowest cost.

With more than 3,200 projects deployed across 43 states and more than 300MW of energized assets constructed, Sparkfund is transforming customer-sited assets into a valuable portfolio resource for the benefit of our society. To learn more about Sparkfund, visit sparkfund.com.

Vice President, Electric Cooperative Markets

Location: Remote, United States
Department: Growth
Reports To: VP, Growth
Employment Type: Full-Time, Exempt
Travel: Frequent, approximately 40%+

About the Role

Sparkfund is looking for a Vice President, Electric Cooperative Markets to own our strategy, positioning, and executive-level relationships across the electric cooperative market and build a meaningful pipeline of Distributed Capacity Procurement opportunities.

This is a strategic individual-contributor role with significant autonomy and enterprise-level influence. While the role does not have direct people-management responsibility, it will represent Sparkfund externally at the executive level and materially influence how we prioritize opportunities, partnerships, and resources across the electric cooperative market.

You will leverage and expand an established network of electric cooperative executives, general managers, board members, and industry leaders to create senior-level access and identify opportunities where Sparkfund can deliver meaningful value. You will work closely with senior commercial leaders to shape account strategy and advance opportunities through proposal development and negotiation, transitioning final deal ownership as opportunities reach the contracting stage.

Success in this role means building a clear and defensible electric cooperative market strategy, materially expanding Sparkfund’s executive-level relationships across the cooperative ecosystem, and creating measurable pipeline influence that converts into signed DCP programs.

How We Work at Sparkfund

Our values shape how we work, make decisions, and show up for our customers and each other. They are also part of how we evaluate success at Sparkfund.

Excellence
We hold ourselves to high standards and continuously look for ways to improve.

Stewardship
We take ownership, follow through on our commitments, and make thoughtful decisions with the long term in mind.

Positivity
We approach challenges constructively, assume positive intent, support one another, and bring solutions.

What You’ll Do

Own Electric Cooperative Market Strategy & Positioning

  • Own Sparkfund’s overall strategy, positioning, and engagement approach for the electric cooperative market.
  • Shape how Sparkfund’s Distributed Capacity Procurement offering is pursued across both distribution and generation and transmission electric cooperatives.
  • Identify and prioritize the highest-value electric cooperative market opportunities and partnerships in coordination with the VP of Growth and executive leadership.
  • Translate market developments, customer needs, and industry dynamics into changes in Sparkfund’s cooperative market strategy and approach.

Build Executive Relationships & Market Access

  • Develop and expand executive-level relationships across the electric cooperative market, leveraging and growing an existing network of cooperative executives, general managers, and board members.
  • Represent Sparkfund externally with cooperative leadership, industry associations, and at conferences and other industry events.
  • Build and maintain relationships across organizations such as NRECA and state and regional electric cooperative associations.
  • Serve as a senior point of access into electric cooperatives, opening doors that materially expand Sparkfund’s addressable cooperative pipeline.

Create and Advance Pipeline

  • Be accountable for creating qualified electric cooperative opportunities and demonstrating measurable pipeline influence against company growth targets.
  • Partner closely with senior commercial leaders to scope opportunities and shape account strategy.
  • Stay actively engaged as opportunities advance through proposal development and negotiation, bringing market knowledge, relationships, and strategic judgment to the process.
  • Transition day-to-day deal ownership as opportunities reach final proposal and contracting stages.
  • Drive the cross-functional strategy and coordination across Growth, Programs, technical teams, and other functions needed to convert cooperative opportunities into signed DCP programs.

Bring Market Insight Into the Business

  • Maintain a current and authoritative understanding of what drives electric cooperatives to pursue new grid capacity solutions.
  • Translate cooperative market insights into Sparkfund’s broader strategy, positioning, and approach.
  • Advise executive leadership on market trends, competitive dynamics, partnership opportunities, and resource allocation decisions affecting Sparkfund’s cooperative growth strategy.

What We’re Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in business development, market development, strategic partnerships, or a related field within the utility, energy, or infrastructure sector.
  • Experience owning and evolving a market, customer segment, or channel strategy end-to-end.
  • An existing, active network of electric cooperative executives, general managers, board members, and/or other senior stakeholders built through prior professional experience in or adjacent to the electric cooperative market.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently establish and evolve market strategy and represent an organization externally at the executive level.
  • Working understanding of electric cooperative governance, member-owned structures, and the factors that influence cooperative purchasing and investment decisions.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence and coordinate work across teams without formal management authority.
  • Ability to travel frequently, approximately 40% or more, to meet with electric cooperative stakeholders and attend industry events.
  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and professional experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience selling, structuring, or developing utility-scale battery storage, generation, distributed capacity, or other grid infrastructure solutions.
  • Familiarity with both generation and transmission and distribution electric cooperative dynamics, including load growth, wholesale power arrangements, and capacity planning.
  • Existing relationships with NRECA and/or state and regional electric cooperative association leadership.
  • Experience driving cross-functional strategy and execution across commercial, program, technical, and operational teams.

What Will Help You Succeed

Market Strategy Ownership
You can set and evolve strategy for an entire market segment, translate changing market conditions into action, and make clear decisions about where the organization should focus.

Executive Relationship Building
You build trust with C-suite, general manager, and board-level stakeholders and can credibly represent Sparkfund as a senior leader in a relationship-driven market.

Cross-Functional Influence
You can align teams around an opportunity and drive progress without relying on direct reporting authority.

Collaborative Account Strategy
You know how to work alongside senior commercial leaders, bring critical market context and judgment into the deal process, and remain actively involved without needing to own every stage of the transaction.

Enterprise Judgment
You operate with significant autonomy, understand when to involve executive leadership, and can advise the business on market priorities and resource allocation with limited day-to-day direction.

Compensation

The expected base pay scale for this role spans from $195,000 to $225,000 per year. Individual placement within the pay band depends on prior experience, technical capabilities, core competencies, positional scope, internal alignment, and related business factors.

Where applicable, this position may also be eligible for discretionary bonus or incentive compensation. Any such compensation is separate from base salary and is not guaranteed. Eligibility, amounts, and payment are subject to applicable plan terms, company performance, individual performance, and other business considerations.

Benefits

Sparkfund offers a competitive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance
  • 401(k) plan with a 2% employer match
  • Flexible vacation policy
  • Paid federal holidays
  • Flexible Fridays, with half-day Fridays every week
  • 12 weeks of gender-neutral paid caregiver leave
  • One-time work-from-home stipend for eligible remote roles
  • $100 monthly phone and internet allowance

Work Environment

Sparkfund is a remote-first company with a distributed workforce. This role is fully remote and may be based anywhere in the United States.

Frequent travel, approximately 40% or more, is expected to meet with electric cooperative executives and other stakeholders, participate in industry conferences and association events, and represent Sparkfund in person.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Sparkfund is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing an inclusive and welcoming environment for all employees and applicants. We do not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, and gender identity), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Sparkfund also provides reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and for sincerely held religious beliefs or practices, in all phases of the hiring process and throughout employment. If you need an accommodation, please let us know.
